projects.name: Repo Intelligence
projects.headline: Ask a codebase how it works. Every claim cites the line it came from.
projects.lede: Point Repo Intelligence at a TypeScript or JavaScript repository and ask something like “explain authentication”. It answers with the files involved, the request flow, the tables and the config, and every claim carries a path:line citation that is re-read from disk before you see it.
projects.status: Private beta, running on my own server.
numbers: dropped claims and the whole answer is refused
problem: Chatting with an LLM about a repository works for questions about one file and fails for questions about a concern. Authentication, for example, is spread across middleware, routes, models, config and utilities, and a chat window only ever sees part of it.

When you're new to a codebase, an answer you have to fact-check yourself is worth less than no answer. So the feature is verifiability, not fluency: every statement points at the exact lines that support it, and the system checks those lines before you read them.
steps: Add a repository
Paste a public git URL. It is shallow-cloned and parsed, about 12 seconds for 2,000 files.
Build the code graph
tree-sitter extracts symbols, imports, calls, routes and ORM models (TypeORM, Drizzle, Sequelize, Prisma) without any LLM calls.
Index it
Code is chunked on symbol boundaries and indexed with BM25, plus optional local embeddings.
Retrieve
Hybrid search finds seed files, then expands along the graph and ranks by role, direction and centrality.
Answer and verify
An LLM writes claims with path:line citations. A validator re-reads every cited span, drops claims that fail, and refuses the answer if more than 30% fail.
capabilities: Citations that are checked
A citation must resolve and the claim's identifiers must actually appear in the cited span, because a line can exist and still not support the claim.
Structure from the code, not the model
Routes, ORM models, request flow and Mermaid diagrams come from resolved graph edges.
Docs are first-class
Markdown and docs are indexed and citable alongside the code.
Measured, not assumed
An eval harness scores retrieval against hand-labelled questions across 4 repos. No ranking change lands without a before-and-after score.
decisions: WASM tree-sitter over native bindings
Native parses 1.7× faster, but parsing isn't the bottleneck and WASM needs no native build toolchain.
Free providers for synthesis
A quality gate that costs money to run doesn't get run, so synthesis goes through my own AI Router over free tiers.
Local embeddings, not hosted
A hosted free tier was measured slower than the local CPU, and it would have sent source code off the machine.
Every ranking change is scored
Changes must move the eval score in the same direction on both labelled strata before they land.
limits: TypeScript and JavaScript only for now.
The evaluation set is small (13 hand-labelled questions), so the graph's extra value is real but not yet stable.
The hosted copy accepts public repositories only.
faq: Can I try it?
The app is in private beta behind a sign-in. If you'd like a walkthrough, get in touch through my portfolio.
Is the code open source?
Not yet. The repository is private.
Does it need an API key?
Retrieval works without one. Writing the answer needs an LLM, which it reaches through AI Router.

projects.name: Smart Trader
projects.headline: An NSE trading desk that backtests first and trades carefully.
projects.lede: A full-stack platform for Indian equities: 31 strategies backtested on NSE history, a live scanner that manages entries, trailing stops and square-off, Telegram alerts, and a tightly guarded executor that places real orders through Dhan.
projects.status: Private app; live execution is supervised and runs on a small account.
numbers: paper trades in one month, profit factor 1.30
risk per real trade, with a daily kill switch
problem: Retail algo trading usually goes one of two ways: backtests that never meet a real market, or live bots that trade before anyone has checked the numbers. Smart Trader is a zero-cost platform that does the boring part first: it backtests every strategy, picks the best one per stock, and watches the live market for setups.
The newer work closes the loop. A heavily guarded adapter places real orders on Dhan for a short whitelist, so real fills can be compared with what the simulator predicted.
steps: Backtest
The Python engine runs strategies over NSE price history and saves a report for each stock.
Activate
A stock, strategy and timeframe that earned it goes on the active list; that list is all the scanner watches.
Scan the market
During market hours the scanner manages open positions and trailing stops, then looks for new setups between 09:30 and the 15:10 square-off.
Signal
Each signal is saved with a simulated trade and pushed to the dashboard over WebSocket and to Telegram.
Execute, carefully
For a whitelisted pair, a market order goes to Dhan and a broker-side protective stop is placed immediately.
capabilities: Strategy library with a backtester
31 strategies, intraday and swing, each backtested before it ever sees live data.
Live scanner and alerts
Entries, trailing stops and exits handled in market hours, with WebSocket and Telegram alerts.
Charts, portfolio and risk
Candlestick charting with portfolio and risk tracking in a React dashboard.
Guarded real-money execution
Fixed 2% risk per trade, a ₹600 daily-loss kill switch, 20 orders a day, and stops that live at the broker.
decisions: Risk is fixed, size flexes
Real position size is the smaller of a risk-based, a notional and a hard quantity cap, so risk stays at 2% whatever the stop distance.
Stops live at the broker
A protective stop-limit rests at Dhan from the first second, so a crash on my side can't leave a position unprotected.
State survives restarts
Positions and the kill switch are stored and reconciled with the broker on boot, after an in-memory map once lost a live position.
Fails safe
If the static-IP proxy that SEBI rules require goes down, orders fail; they never bypass it.
limits: Real-money trading is at an early validation stage on a small account. It is not a proven autonomous system.
Real execution is cash-equity intraday only, and exits can lag the market by up to about 100 seconds.
Paper results are before real costs, so live net returns will trail the simulation.
faq: Can I use it?
The app is private. The source is public on GitHub if you'd like to read how it works.
Does it trade real money?
Yes, narrowly: two whitelisted intraday pairs on a small, supervised account. Everything else is simulated.
Is this investment advice?
No. It's an engineering project, and its own docs say not to treat it as a proven system.

projects.name: Crypto AI
projects.headline: A crypto futures lab that paper-trades before risking a rupee.
projects.lede: Crypto AI analyses BTC, ETH and SOL perpetuals on Binance, generates signals from 12 strategies and paper-trades them with 1,00,000 of virtual capital, so every strategy is tested on the live market before real money is involved.
projects.status: Paper trading only. Live trading is a deliberately gated final phase.
numbers: daily-loss kill switch on the paper account
problem: Leveraged crypto futures punish untested ideas quickly. Crypto AI exists to test first: it runs strategies against the live market with virtual capital for about a month before any real money is risked.
Everything uses free data sources (Binance public data, CoinGecko, Fear & Greed, RSS news), so the whole experiment costs nothing to run.
steps: Backtest
Run a strategy with slippage and funding costs, compare Sharpe, Sortino and Calmar with buy-and-hold, then promote it to live.
Scan
Every 60 seconds the scanner runs promoted strategies and emits entry, stop, target, reward-to-risk and confidence.
Filter
An optional meta-label model only lets through signals with a predicted win probability of at least 55%.
Paper trade
A paper broker opens positions under risk limits and manages trailing stops and the kill switch.
Learn, with approval
The agent proposes bounded changes from regime and performance analysis; I approve, reject or revert each one.
capabilities: One strategy code path
The same functions drive backtests and live signals, so a backtested edge behaves the same live.
Backtests that try to break
Slippage and funding, parameter sweeps, out-of-sample and walk-forward tests, and Monte Carlo.
A paper broker with real rules
Up to 30× leverage, 1% risk per trade, 5 open positions at most, and a daily-loss kill switch.
Market intelligence
Funding rate, open interest, long/short ratio, BTC dominance and a correlation matrix on the dashboard.
decisions: Hand-rolled indicators
pandas-ta breaks on NumPy 2, so indicators are written by hand and tested.
The broker is an interface
A future live broker plugs in without touching the portfolio's risk logic.
Propose, then approve
The adaptive layer changes nothing on its own, and flags results that look too good (win rate above 80%, profit factor above 4) as likely overfitting.
Rules before models for regimes
Regimes come from ADX, EMA slope and ATR rules: transparent, and they need no training data.
limits: Paper trading only. The live broker phase is not built.
Live results are expected to trail backtests, and the meta-label model needs about 100 trades before it can train.
The AI commentary needs free-tier API keys and switches off without them.
faq: Can I use it?
The hosted app is private, but the source is public on GitHub and runs locally with one command.
Does it trade real money?
No. It is paper only, and the agent never trades on its own.
What does the AI do?
It writes market commentary, explains backtests and answers portfolio questions. It never sizes or places a trade.

projects.name: AI Router
projects.headline: One OpenAI-compatible endpoint in front of many AI providers.
projects.lede: A self-hosted gateway that routes chat, embeddings, images, speech and more across mostly free-tier providers. Point the standard openai SDK at it, ask for model "auto", and it picks a healthy, well-scoring model and fails over before you notice. It serves 5 of my live projects.
projects.status: Live. API keys are issued per project; there is no public sign-up.
numbers: exploration so new models get a chance
problem: Across my projects the same free API keys were wired in by hand, and the fallback loop had been written nine times, in two languages, with three contradicting failover policies.

Worse, model IDs rot silently. Twelve models in one provider's catalogue returned 410 Gone, and ten of fourteen IDs at another no longer existed. Published metadata about free AI is unreliable; only probing tells the truth. AI Router does that work once, for every project.
steps: Call it like OpenAI
Any project sends a standard request with the stock SDK. The model field is a routing hint: auto, a task, or a pinned model.
Resolve a chain
The router builds the candidate list for that task, ordered by live health and measured quality.
Try within one budget
Each hop gets what's left of a single wall-clock budget, so retries can never stack up past the deadline.
Validate the output
Structured output is checked against the JSON schema, repaired once, and escalated to the next model if it still fails.
Learn from the outcome
Every result updates the health table and the per-task scorecard, and models that keep failing a task are demoted.
capabilities: Drop-in compatible
Chat, structured JSON, streaming, tools, vision, embeddings, rerank, images, speech and transcription through one API.
Health known before requests
A background prober checks one stale model per tick, so health is known without burning free quota.
Routing on measured quality
Models are scored on first-try schema validity, success rate and latency, with a minimum sample before a score counts.
Failures with names
Empty replies, schema failures and retired models are typed outcomes, so they can be counted and fixed.
decisions: Probes can't promote
A probe can only lift a model to 'unknown'; only real traffic earns 'ready'.
Never cross embedding dimensions
A 768-wide vector where 1024 was promised would silently poison a search index, so fallback stays within one dimension.
Streams fail over before the first token only
Once bytes are on the wire it's a pipe; switching models mid-answer would corrupt it.
The paid fallback is fenced in code
The one metered provider is last-hop only, never probed, allow-listed and capped per day.
limits: It runs on a single home server, which is a single point of failure.
Free tiers churn constantly, so some providers answer only part of the time.
It's for my own projects: keys are minted per project and there's no public access.
faq: Can I get a key?
Not at the moment. It serves my own projects, and keys are issued per project.
Is it really free?
Mostly. One metered provider is kept as a capped, last-resort fallback.
Why a service and not a library?
My projects are split between TypeScript and Python, and routing lives in the model string, so any stock OpenAI SDK can drive it.
